correctness.rationale: In an abelian group G of exponent m, a term equation is a linear word with integer coefficients c_i. Its image G^k->G is dG for d=gcd(m,c_1,...,c_k) by Bezout, so its satisfaction probability is 1/|dG|=|G[d]|/|G|; every divisor d|m occurs as dx=0, and multiplication-only terms realize the same equation spectrum. Under primary cyclic decomposition, |G[p^j]|=p^{f_p(j)} with increments f_p(j)-f_p(j-1)=number of elementary cyclic factors of length >=j, a positive weakly decreasing sequence. The normalized spectrum separates prime-power exponents and the independent CRT combinations, so differences reconstruct each conjugate partition and conversely characterize realizable rational sets. The identity group N=1 is handled separately. Independent exact test reconstructed sample distinct abelian groups and subgroup-kernel sizes, not relied on as unrestricted proof.

A primary-profile inverse theorem may be implicitly classical under torsion-size distribution; this is retained as residual risk.
